gap: Atmosphere and sun (A): from about 110 m altitude, the skyline across the water (about 1-2 km away) must show clear aerial perspective. It must look visibly lower in contrast and tinted toward the haze or sky colour compared with the blocks directly under the helicopter. The sky must show clouds or a visible sun with bloom. The bay water must reflect the skyline and sky with a sun glint, not read as a flat uniform grey-blue plane.

Judge: The commercial frames win all four pairs by a wide margin. B wins pairs 1-2 and A wins pairs 3-4. Three of the four commercial frames genuinely wow: the helicopter shot in haze, the hillside view with the sun behind the city, and the dusk freeway. The fourth, the golf course, is polished but not striking. No in-dev frame wows. The in-dev game frames everything well and its landmarks are recognisable, but it fails in the same ways in every pair. Lighting is flat and mostly ambient, with no aerial perspective, so distant towers are as crisp as nearby ones. Skies are pale gradients. Water and ground are matte, untextured planes. Buildings are extruded boxes with tiling window textures, and shophouse rows are copy-pasted. Streets are almost empty, with no visible crowds. The edge of the world shows: open sea and a hard horizon sit right behind the skyline. The HUD is cluttered, with a placeholder grid minimap and a captured mouse cursor. Its best frames are pair 4 (warm low sun, a decent character and foliage) and pair 3 (directional shadows), but even those lack traffic, surface detail and depth layering. Suggested priority order: (1) atmospheric perspective plus a real sun and sky; (2) traffic and pedestrian density; (3) ground and water materials with reflections; (4) filling the background so the city recedes into haze instead of ending at the sea.
